headline: Oak Hill Road approved for Merrimack Valley School District; Garrison Park pool approved for demolition.
summary: The council also approved an $8,300 golf reserve and moved $70,589.24 in opioid settlement money to a reserve. It made a part-time Human Resources job full-time and added penalties to the demolition review ordinance. It tabled the West Street Ward House decision and sent social district rules to a committee.
decisions: Approved the consent calendar, with the pulled items taken off.
Approved moving $70,589.24 in litigation settlement funds into the Opioid Abatement Reserve.
Approved a Golf Course Improvement Reserve and an $8,300 transfer into it.
Approved the petition to restore Oak Hill Road to the Merrimack Valley School District.
Approved changing the Administrative Coordinator job in Human Resources from part-time to full-time.
Approved adding penalties to the demolition review ordinance, Article 26-9.
Tabled the West Street Ward House repair and future-use report so staff can gather public input.
Motion to table the Garrison Park pool failed for lack of a second.
Approved going forward with demolition of the Garrison Park pool.
Approved the quarterly status report on the City Council's 2026-27 priorities.
Approved the Public Safety Advisory Board's recommendation to develop a memorandum of understanding for emergency cooling centers.
Approved council conduct guidelines for interactions with staff and commissions.
Approved the September 30th, 2026 fiscal year-to-date financial statements.
Approved the June 30th, 2026 trust fund reports, MS-9 and MS-10.
Referred social district rules and application procedures to the Economic Development Advisory Committee.
Approved the city manager applying to the Mapillary camera grant program 3.0.
Approved directing the tax collector not to execute tax deeds on certain properties.
discussion: Golf course reserve: Speakers questioned whether non-resident golf fees were meant for a separate reserve, and some urged using them to pay clubhouse bonds or the general fund.

West Street Ward House: Repairs are estimated at about $750,000, mostly for a slate roof. Options discussed included repairs, a sale, and higher rental rates, and the council tabled the item for public input.
Garrison Park pool: The pool has been open only once in five years, mainly because of staffing problems. Residents had asked to keep it as a pool, and the council voted to go forward with demolition.
Demolition review penalties: Staff said penalties would be rarely used, mainly for flagrant violations, with fines up to $500 under the city charter and civil penalties of $275 for a first offense.
Human Resources position: Members debated whether to address the class and compensation study before adding staff. Staff cited upcoming retirements as the reason for the full-time change.
